exampleSentences: With an RPO of five minutes, we need continuous replication rather than nightly backups.
An RPO of zero usually means synchronous replication across regions.

defCn: 可用性，系统能够正常提供服务的时间占比
defEn: The proportion of time a system is operational and able to serve requests.
exampleSentence: Replicating across three zones improved our availability during single-zone failures.
exampleSentences: Replicating across three zones improved our availability during single-zone failures.
Availability is a product decision as much as an engineering one.

defCn: 可用时长，系统连续正常运行的时间
defEn: The amount of time a system has been running without downtime.
codeExample: Uptime: 99.98% over 90 days (13 minutes of downtime)
exampleSentence: We advertise 99.95% uptime, which is roughly four hours of downtime a year.
exampleSentences: We advertise 99.95% uptime, which is roughly four hours of downtime a year.
Chasing perfect uptime is expensive; spend the error budget instead.

defCn: 兜底回退，下游失败时改用备用路径或返回降级结果
defEn: A backup behaviour used when a dependency fails, such as returning cached or default data.
codeExample: try { return svc.recommend(id); } catch { return CACHE.popular(); // fallback }
exampleSentence: When the recommendation service is down, the fallback returns the most popular items.
exampleSentences: When the recommendation service is down, the fallback returns the most popular items.
Every fallback must itself be cheap, or it becomes the next outage.
A stale cache is a better fallback than an error page.

defCn: 指数退避，重试间隔按指数递增，避免把正在恢复的服务再次打垮
defEn: A retry strategy where the wait between attempts grows exponentially.
exampleSentence: The client uses exponential backoff so a recovering service is not swamped by retries.
exampleSentences: The client uses exponential backoff so a recovering service is not swamped by retries.
Always add jitter to exponential backoff, or all clients retry in lockstep.
We cap exponential backoff at 30 seconds and then give up.

defCn: 对冲请求，原请求迟迟未返回时再发一个副本，取先返回的结果
defEn: A duplicate request sent when the original is slow, taking whichever response returns first.
codeExample: if (!resp && elapsed > p95) send(hedgedRequest);  // hedged request
exampleSentence: A hedged request cut our p99 in half, at the cost of a few percent extra traffic.
exampleSentences: A hedged request cut our p99 in half, at the cost of a few percent extra traffic.
Only send a hedged request for reads, never for writes.

defCn: 截止时间，随请求向下传递的剩余时间预算，过期即放弃后续工作
defEn: A time budget propagated with a request; downstream calls give up once it expires.
exampleSentence: Passing a deadline down the call chain stops us from waiting on work the user has already abandoned.
exampleSentences: Passing a deadline down the call chain stops us from waiting on work the user has already abandoned.
Each hop subtracts its own cost before forwarding the deadline.

defCn: N+1 查询问题，先查列表再逐条查询，查询次数随数据量线性膨胀
defEn: The anti-pattern of fetching a list and then issuing one extra query per row.
codeExample: SELECT * FROM orders;  -- then: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?  (N+1 query)
exampleSentence: The N+1 query was fine with ten rows in dev and a meltdown with ten thousand in production.
exampleSentences: The N+1 query was fine with ten rows in dev and a meltdown with ten thousand in production.
A join or a batched IN clause removes the N+1 query entirely.

defCn: 连接池耗尽，可用连接全部被占满，新请求拿不到连接
defEn: The state where every pooled connection is in use, so new requests cannot get one.
codeExample: pool: maxSize=20, inUse=20, waiting=340  // connection pool exhaustion
exampleSentence: A missing statement timeout is the usual cause of connection pool exhaustion.
exampleSentences: A missing statement timeout is the usual cause of connection pool exhaustion.
A five-second statement timeout prevents connection pool exhaustion better than a bigger pool.

defCn: 乐观锁，用版本号或时间戳检测并发冲突，冲突时才失败并重试
defEn: Concurrency control that detects conflicts with a version field instead of locking rows.
codeExample: UPDATE items SET qty=9, version=6 WHERE id=1 AND version=5; -- optimistic locking
exampleSentence: With optimistic locking, the second writer fails the version check instead of silently overwriting the first.
exampleSentences: With optimistic locking, the second writer fails the version check instead of silently overwriting the first.
Optimistic locking wins when conflicts are rare and retries are cheap.

defCn: 悲观锁，先加锁再修改，其他事务必须等待锁释放
defEn: Concurrency control that locks a row before modifying it, making other writers wait.
codeExample: SELECT * FROM seats WHERE id=7 FOR UPDATE;  -- pessimistic locking
exampleSentence: Frequent conflicts justify pessimistic locking, because retries would be wasteful.
exampleSentences: Frequent conflicts justify pessimistic locking, because retries would be wasteful.
Use pessimistic locking when conflicts are frequent and retries would be wasteful.

defCn: 多版本并发控制，通过保留数据的多个版本让读不阻塞写、写不阻塞读
defEn: Multiversion Concurrency Control: keeping multiple row versions so readers and writers don't block each other.
codeExample: SELECT * FROM orders AS OF snapshot_12345;  -- MVCC snapshot read
exampleSentence: MVCC is why a long-running report in Postgres does not block incoming writes.
exampleSentences: MVCC is why a long-running report in Postgres does not block incoming writes.
MVCC gives every transaction its own snapshot of the data.

defCn: 死锁，两个及以上事务互相持有对方需要的锁而永久等待
defEn: A state where two or more transactions each hold a lock the other needs, so none can proceed.
codeExample: ERROR 1213 (40001): Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction
exampleSentence: Updating the two rows in opposite orders caused a deadlock under load.
exampleSentences: Updating the two rows in opposite orders caused a deadlock under load.
Always acquire locks in a consistent order to avoid a deadlock.
The database killed one victim to break the deadlock and the client retried.

defCn: 锁竞争，大量事务争抢同一把锁导致彼此等待、吞吐被压低
defEn: Heavy competition for the same lock, causing transactions to wait and throughput to drop.
codeExample: // every checkout locks the same inventory row -> lock contention
exampleSentence: Sharding the counter removed the lock contention without changing the business logic.
exampleSentences: Sharding the counter removed the lock contention without changing the business logic.
Sharding the counter removed the lock contention without changing the business logic.

defCn: 脏读，读到了另一个事务尚未提交、随时可能被回滚的数据
defEn: Reading data written by a transaction that has not committed and may still roll back.
codeExample: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ UNCOMMITTED;  -- allows dirty read
exampleSentence: A dirty read showed a balance that was rolled back a millisecond later.
exampleSentences: A dirty read showed a balance that was rolled back a millisecond later.
READ COMMITTED removes the dirty read but not the non-repeatable read.

defCn: 幻读，同一事务内两次范围查询返回了不同行数，因为别的事务插入了新行
defEn: A second range query in the same transaction returning new rows inserted by another transaction.
codeExample: SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE amount > 100;  -- 42, then 43: phantom read
exampleSentence: Raising the isolation level to serializable eliminated the phantom read in the reconciliation job.
exampleSentences: Raising the isolation level to serializable eliminated the phantom read in the reconciliation job.
A phantom read is about new rows appearing, not about existing rows changing.

defCn: 隔离级别，数据库对并发事务相互可见程度的设定，从读未提交到可串行化
defEn: The database setting controlling how much concurrent transactions see of each other's work.
codeExample: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;
exampleSentence: We lowered the isolation level to read committed to get the throughput we needed.
exampleSentences: We lowered the isolation level to read committed to get the throughput we needed.
Every isolation level above read committed costs you some concurrency.

defCn: 两阶段提交，跨多个资源的分布式事务协议，先投票准备再统一提交
defEn: A distributed transaction protocol with a prepare-vote phase followed by a commit phase.
codeExample:
PREPARE TRANSACTION 'tx1';  -- phase 1
COMMIT PREPARED 'tx1';      -- phase 2
exampleSentence: Most teams replace two-phase commit with a saga to avoid holding locks across services.
exampleSentences: Most teams replace two-phase commit with a saga to avoid holding locks across services.
Most teams replace two-phase commit with a saga to avoid holding locks across services.

defCn: 丢失更新，两个事务并发读写同一行，后写的把先写的修改覆盖掉
defEn: Two concurrent read-modify-write cycles where the second silently overwrites the first.
codeExample: // both read qty=10, both write qty=9: one update is lost
exampleSentence: The lost update happened because neither request used a transaction or a version check.
exampleSentences: The lost update happened because neither request used a transaction or a version check.
An atomic UPDATE ... SET qty = qty - 1 avoids the lost update entirely.

defCn: 复制，把数据同步拷贝到多个节点以提高可用性和读吞吐
defEn: Copying data to multiple nodes to improve availability and read throughput.
exampleSentence: Asynchronous replication means a failover can lose the last few commits.
exampleSentences: Asynchronous replication means a failover can lose the last few commits.
Asynchronous replication means a failover can lose the last few commits.

defCn: 领导者选举，集群在多数派同意下选出唯一负责协调写入的节点
defEn: The process by which a cluster picks one node, with quorum agreement, to coordinate writes.
codeExample: etcdctl endpoint status  -- leader election picks one node per term
exampleSentence: After the crash, leader election finished in three seconds and writes resumed.
exampleSentences: After the crash, leader election finished in three seconds and writes resumed.
Leader election needs an odd number of nodes so a majority always exists.

defCn: 共识，多个节点在存在故障和网络延迟的情况下对某个值或顺序达成一致
defEn: The problem of getting distributed nodes to agree on a value or an ordering despite failures.
exampleSentence: You cannot hand-roll consensus correctly; use Raft.
exampleSentences: You cannot hand-roll consensus correctly; use Raft.
You cannot hand-roll consensus correctly; use Raft.

defCn: Raft 共识算法，通过领导者选举和日志复制让多节点达成一致，比 Paxos 更易理解
defEn: A consensus algorithm based on leader election and log replication, designed to be easier to understand than Paxos.
exampleSentence: We chose Raft because our team could actually reason about it during an incident.
exampleSentences: We chose Raft because our team could actually reason about it during an incident.
Raft splits consensus into leader election, log replication, and safety.

defCn: 脑裂，网络分区后两侧都以为自己是主节点并同时接受写入
defEn: A failure where a network partition leaves two nodes believing they are the leader and both accept writes.
codeExample: // partition: node-A and node-B both promote themselves -> split brain
exampleSentence: A fencing token is the usual defence against split brain.
exampleSentences: A fencing token is the usual defence against split brain.
A fencing token is the usual defence against split brain.

defCn: 一致性哈希，节点增减时只需迁移少量键的哈希分配方式
defEn: A hashing scheme where adding or removing a node remaps only a small fraction of keys.
codeExample: ring.Add(node)  // consistent hashing: only K/N keys move
exampleSentence: Virtual nodes make consistent hashing distribute load evenly.
exampleSentences: Virtual nodes make consistent hashing distribute load evenly.
Virtual nodes make consistent hashing distribute load evenly.

defCn: CAP 定理，网络分区发生时一致性（C）与可用性（A）不可兼得
defEn: The theorem that during a network partition a system must choose between consistency and availability.
codeExample: // P happens -> pick C (reject writes) or pick A (serve stale)
exampleSentence: CAP theorem forces a real choice: we drop availability to stay consistent.
exampleSentences: CAP theorem forces a real choice: we drop availability to stay consistent.
CAP theorem is not about normal operation, only about what you do during a partition.

defCn: 预写日志，修改数据前先落盘的日志，用于崩溃恢复和主从复制
defEn: A log written to durable storage before the data is modified, used for crash recovery and replication.
codeExample: WAL: [LSN 1001 COMMIT tx7] -> flush -> apply to pages
exampleSentence: The write-ahead log is why the database can replay committed transactions after a crash.
exampleSentences: The write-ahead log is why the database can replay committed transactions after a crash.
Group commit batches fsyncs on the write-ahead log to save disk I/O.

defCn: 至少一次投递，消息保证不丢但可能重复，因此消费者必须幂等
defEn: A delivery guarantee where messages are never lost but may be delivered more than once.
codeExample: // at-least-once delivery: ack only after processing succeeds
exampleSentence: With at-least-once delivery, the consumer has to be idempotent.
exampleSentences: With at-least-once delivery, the consumer has to be idempotent.
At-least-once delivery plus an idempotency key behaves like exactly-once to the user.

defCn: 至多一次投递，消息绝不重复但可能因失败而丢失
defEn: A delivery guarantee where messages are never duplicated but may be lost.
codeExample: // at-most-once delivery: ack before processing, never retry
exampleSentence: Fire-and-forget UDP gives you at-most-once delivery.
exampleSentences: Fire-and-forget UDP gives you at-most-once delivery.
Fire-and-forget UDP gives you at-most-once delivery.

defCn: 恰好一次语义，对外表现为每条消息只被处理一次，通常由幂等加事务实现
defEn: The guarantee that each message is processed exactly once, usually built from idempotence plus transactions.
exampleSentence: Vendors sell exactly-once semantics, but you still need a dedupe key at the sink.
exampleSentences: Vendors sell exactly-once semantics, but you still need a dedupe key at the sink.
Vendors sell exactly-once semantics, but you still need a dedupe key at the sink.

defCn: 双写，同时写数据库和消息中间件但不在一个事务里，崩溃会造成两边不一致
defEn: Writing to two systems, such as a database and a broker, outside a single transaction.
codeExample:
db.insert(order);      // 1
broker.publish(event); // 2 -- crash here = dual write problem
exampleSentence: The dual write crashed between the two steps and left orders that were never fulfilled.
exampleSentences: The dual write crashed between the two steps and left orders that were never fulfilled.
The transactional outbox pattern exists to eliminate the dual write.

defCn: 有害消息，反复处理失败、会一直卡住消费者的消息
defEn: A message that always fails processing and would otherwise block the consumer forever.
codeExample: if (attempts >= 3) deadLetter(msg);  // treat as poison message
exampleSentence: We send any poison message to the dead-letter queue after three failed attempts.
exampleSentences: We send any poison message to the dead-letter queue after three failed attempts.
One poison message with a malformed payload stalled the whole consumer group.

defCn: 重放，把历史事件或消息重新处理一遍以修复数据或重建状态
defEn: Re-processing stored events or messages to repair data or rebuild state.
exampleSentence: A replay of yesterday's events rebuilt the read model in ten minutes.
exampleSentences: A replay of yesterday's events rebuilt the read model in ten minutes.
We replayed yesterday's events into a new read model after the bug fix.

defCn: 协同式协作，各服务通过事件自发响应，没有中心协调者
defEn: A coordination style where services react to each other's events with no central orchestrator.
codeExample: OrderPlaced -> payment svc, inventory svc, email svc  // choreography
exampleSentence: We moved from choreography to an orchestrator when the flow needed a compensating step.
exampleSentences: We moved from choreography to an orchestrator when the flow needed a compensating step.
We moved from choreography to an orchestrator when the flow needed a compensating step.

defCn: 事件溯源，用不可变事件序列作为唯一事实来源，当前状态由事件推演得出
defEn: Storing every change as an immutable event and deriving current state by replaying them.
codeExample: events: [Created, Renamed, Shipped]  ->  fold()  ->  current state
exampleSentence: That is why event sourcing pairs naturally with CQRS.
exampleSentences: That is why event sourcing pairs naturally with CQRS.
Event sourcing pairs naturally with CQRS: events are written, projections are read.

defCn: 物化视图，把查询结果实体化存储的视图，读取快但需要用刷新换取新鲜度
defEn: A view whose result is stored on disk, trading refresh cost for fast reads.
codeExample: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW daily_revenue AS SELECT ...;
exampleSentence: A materialized view turned a thirty-second aggregate into a millisecond lookup.
exampleSentences: A materialized view turned a thirty-second aggregate into a millisecond lookup.
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY keeps it readable during the refresh.

defCn: 反规范化，有意保留冗余数据以换取更快的读取
defEn: Intentionally duplicating data to make reads faster.
exampleSentence: Every denormalization buys read speed with a new consistency obligation.
exampleSentences: Every denormalization buys read speed with a new consistency obligation.
Every denormalization buys read speed with a new consistency obligation.

defCn: upsert，存在则更新、不存在则插入的合并写入操作
defEn: A write operation that inserts the row if it is missing and updates it if it exists.
codeExample:
INSERT INTO counters (k, v) VALUES ('pv', 1)
  ON CONFLICT (k) DO UPDATE SET v = counters.v + 1;  -- upsert
exampleSentence: An upsert makes the endpoint idempotent without a separate existence check.
exampleSentences: An upsert makes the endpoint idempotent without a separate existence check.
The upsert removed the last race condition in the sync job.

defCn: 只读副本，承载读流量的从库副本，用于扩展读吞吐
defEn: A read-only copy of the primary database used to scale read traffic.
exampleSentence: We pointed the reporting queries at a read replica so they stopped slowing down checkout.
exampleSentences: We pointed the reporting queries at a read replica so they stopped slowing down checkout.
A read replica lags the primary by a second, so read-your-writes can break.

defCn: 复合索引，按多列顺序建立的索引，列顺序决定它能服务哪些查询
defEn: An index built over multiple columns, whose column order determines which queries it can serve.
codeExample: CREATE INDEX ON events (tenant_id, created_at DESC);  -- composite index
exampleSentence: A composite index on (tenant_id, created_at) finally made the paged query use an index scan.
exampleSentences: A composite index on (tenant_id, created_at) finally made the paged query use an index scan.
Column order in a composite index follows the leftmost-prefix rule.

defCn: 写放大，一次逻辑写入在底层引发多次物理写入
defEn: One logical write causing many physical writes underneath.
codeExample: 1 row update -> 4 index updates + 1 WAL flush  // write amplification
exampleSentence: Too many indexes turn every insert into serious write amplification.
exampleSentences: Too many indexes turn every insert into serious write amplification.
Too many indexes turn every insert into serious write amplification.

defCn: 远程过程调用，像调用本地方法一样调用另一台机器上的服务
defEn: Remote Procedure Call: invoking a function on another machine as if it were local.
exampleSentence: Every RPC needs a timeout, because the network will eventually fail.
exampleSentences: Every RPC needs a timeout, because the network will eventually fail.
Treat an RPC as a remote call, not a local one: it can be slow, absent, or duplicated.

defCn: 编组，把内存中的对象转换成可传输或可存储的格式（常与序列化同义）
defEn: Converting an in-memory object into a format suitable for transmission or storage.
codeExample: json.Marshal(order)  // marshalling an object to bytes
exampleSentence: In our service, marshalling is the outgoing direction and unmarshalling the incoming one.
exampleSentences: In our service, marshalling is the outgoing direction and unmarshalling the incoming one.
Marshalling is the outgoing direction; unmarshalling is the incoming one.

defCn: 线程池，复用固定数量的线程执行任务，避免频繁创建销毁线程
defEn: A fixed set of reusable threads for executing tasks instead of creating one per task.
exampleSentence: Sizing the thread pool too small turned spare CPU into pure queueing delay.
exampleSentences: Sizing the thread pool too small turned spare CPU into pure queueing delay.
A separate thread pool per dependency keeps one slow client from starving the others.

defCn: 心跳，节点周期性发出的存活信号，用于判断节点是否失效
defEn: A periodic signal from a node indicating that it is still alive.
exampleSentence: Three missed heartbeat intervals and the node is marked dead and its work reassigned.
exampleSentences: Three missed heartbeat intervals and the node is marked dead and its work reassigned.
A missed heartbeat is a suspicion, not a proof, that the node is gone.

defCn: 埋点插桩，在代码中采集指标、日志和链路数据的能力
defEn: The code that emits metrics, logs, and traces so the system can be observed.
exampleSentence: Without instrumentation, every incident turns into guesswork.
exampleSentences: Without instrumentation, every incident turns into guesswork.
Add instrumentation at the edges first: the handler and every outbound call.

defCn: span，链路追踪中的一个工作单元，表示一次调用及其耗时
defEn: A single timed unit of work within a distributed trace.
exampleSentence: Each span in the trace shows one hop and how long it waited.
exampleSentences: Each span in the trace shows one hop and how long it waited.
A span carries a parent id, so a trace can be reassembled from spans.

defCn: 链路，一次请求在各服务间流转形成的完整调用链，由多个 span 组成
defEn: The end-to-end record of one request as it travels across services, made of spans.
exampleSentence: The trace showed 900 ms of the 1 s request spent in one downstream call.
exampleSentences: The trace showed 900 ms of the 1 s request spent in one downstream call.
Pass the trace id in every request so you can stitch the spans together.

defCn: 告警，指标越过阈值时自动通知值班人员
defEn: Automatically notifying on-call engineers when a metric crosses a threshold.
exampleSentence: Good alerting pages a human only when a user is actually being hurt.
exampleSentences: Good alerting pages a human only when a user is actually being hurt.
Most alerting pain comes from alerting on causes instead of symptoms.

defCn: 自动扩缩容，根据负载指标自动增减实例数量
defEn: Automatically adding or removing instances based on load metrics.
exampleSentence: Keep a warm baseline, because autoscaling on CPU alone misses I/O-bound services.
exampleSentences: Keep a warm baseline, because autoscaling on CPU alone misses I/O-bound services.
Autoscaling on CPU alone misses services that are I/O bound.

defCn: 容量规划，预测未来负载并提前准备相应的资源
defEn: Estimating future load and provisioning resources ahead of it.
codeExample: peak 12k rps / 800 rps per node = 15 nodes + 30% headroom
exampleSentence: Good capacity planning starts with a rough peak estimate, not with a benchmark.
exampleSentences: Good capacity planning starts with a rough peak estimate, not with a benchmark.
Capacity planning starts with a rough peak estimate, not with a benchmark.
